newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala refugees blast delay of their return.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala refugees blast delay of their return.

text.p: A group of 600 refugees living in Mexico threatened on Friday to occupy a Guatemalan consulate and return to Guatemala prematurely if the government does not fulfil its promise to buy land for them.

"Since last year the return date has been postponed again and again. It's been too long. What we are demanding is the immediate purchase of the farm that has been promised," Carlos Choc of the Permanent Commissions Representing Guatemalan Refugees in Mexico, told reporters on Friday.

The refugees threatened to take over the Guatemalan consulate in Chetumal, in Quintana Roo state, on the Caribbean Sea -- the same consulate that was overrun for two days by the same protesters in December, Choc said.

In the early 1980s, at the height of Guatemala's violent 36-year civil war, tens of thousands of Guatemalans, mostly poor Indians from the wartorn highland regions, fled to southern Mexico. The war ended with a Dec. 29, 1996, peace accord.
More than 31,787 refugees returned to Guatemala under special agreements with the government, which purchased farms for groups of returnees.
After signing the peace treaty with leftist rebels, the government announced plans to complete repatriation programmes this year, bringing home an additional 12,000 people.

But refugee groups frequently complained that negotiations for their return dragged on too long. The government, however, alleged refugees backed out of promises to return after land was bought for them.
